The first experiment produced results where most mechanisms fit similarly well (NLL around -21.4). This is expected for a single baseline curve — many mechanisms can fit simple kinetics. M5 (extra intermediate) and M4 (alternate catalytic species X) fit poorly. The rest are essentially indistinguishable at this stage. We need to design experiments that push mechanistic differences to the fore.
</reflection>

<hypothesis>
Key differences among remaining candidates:
- Catalyst deactivation pathways (M9-M20): different dependencies on [S], [P], [cat], [catS]
- Dimerization (M2, M3, M13): [cat]^2 dependence  
- Product inhibition (M12, M17): depend on [P]
- Substrate inhibition (M11, M16): depend on [S]
- Ligand dissociation/activation (M6, M8): depend on catalyst pre-equilibrium

To discriminate:
- Varying [cat] tests dimerization (M2, M3, M13, M18, M19) - these predict non-linear rate scaling with [cat]
- Adding initial product tests product inhibition (M12, M17) 
- Varying [S] tests substrate inhibition (M11, M16, M7)

For maximum discrimination, I'll increase [cat] significantly (10x). This tests:
- M1, M14, M9, others linear in cat: rate scales linearly
- M2, M3, M13: dimerization sequesters catalyst → sublinear scaling
- M18, M19: 2catS or cat+catS deactivation → faster deactivation at high [cat]
- M6, M8: activation via ligand loss → non-linear effects

Also using low [S] to avoid quick depletion and see catalyst behavior clearly.
</hypothesis>
